payload.affects: governance and measurement; NOT economic behaviour
payload.correction: session-run.ps1 no longer passes --interval or --period to autotrade, so the CLI defaults (1d, 2y) apply and the effective configuration hashes to da22011e.... Changing only --interval would have left ~24 daily bars against a minimum_history of 50 and silently stopped all trading.
payload.evidence: scripts/preoos_interval_equivalence.py, 2026-09-21: 230/230 symbols passed the gate under both configurations, no symbol had fewer than the rule's 215 daily bars, and the candidate set was identical (BAC, CVS, KRE, RTX, UNP).
payload.reports_affected: none invalidated; the published digest is restored, not changed
payload.title: Runner passed --interval 15m; fingerprint hashed defaults
payload.what_was_wrong: frozen_fingerprint() digested AutoTradeConfig() defaults, where interval='1d', while session-run.ps1 passed --interval 15m --period 1mo. The live configuration hashed to 569a8da7..., not the published da22011e.... Both sides of every check read the same defaults, so the divergence was undetectable.

payload.correction: forward.config_digest() is now one definition with parameters; frozen_fingerprint() is config_digest() with no arguments. run_once logs config_digest(...) of the objects it actually ran on into its run_complete event. The recorder stamps the observation with THAT value and refuses to record when it differs from the declared frozen fingerprint.
payload.title: Fingerprint is now an observation of the run (Option C)
payload.what_was_wrong: The stamp on a clean observation was recomputed from source defaults by the recorder, so it could never disagree with the source and could never detect what the trading process did.

payload.correction: The benchmark now uses adjustment='all', matching the declaration already inside the digest, so the fingerprint is untouched. The split-adjusted pair is stored beside it and both closes used are recorded, because an adjusted series is restated by the vendor on every distribution.
payload.reports_affected: none; the recorder has produced zero observations
payload.title: Benchmark compared total return against SPY price return
payload.what_was_wrong: record_clean_session fetched SPY with the default adjustment='split' and compared a PRICE return against the account's TOTAL return, while the fingerprint declared basis_post_2016='total_vs_total'. SPY price return understates its total return by about 1.58 points a year.

payload.correction: A whitelisted projection is now recorded per position: symbol, quantity, market value, average entry price, unrealised P&L, whether a protective stop rests, and its stop price. No account identifier, no order id.
payload.title: CleanObservation.positions was never populated
payload.what_was_wrong: The field exists because 'a count cannot be checked against a sizing rule', but build_observation never passed it, so every observation would have recorded a position count and no per-name sizes.

payload.correction: crypto_market_value, parking_market_value, reserved_fraction, cash_movements, equity_sleeve_equity and equity_sleeve_return are now recorded. equity_sleeve_return is the HEADLINE candidate metric and is net of external cash movement; strategy_return keeps its original name and meaning - the combined account - rather than being silently repurposed.
payload.title: Account-level return conflated the equity book with a live BTC sleeve
payload.what_was_wrong: strategy_return was account equity over prior account equity, and the account holds a live BTC sleeve (about 5.6% of equity, traded every 30 seconds) plus parked cash. The recorded return was therefore not the frozen candidate's return, and no crypto position was recorded, so the two could not be separated.

payload.correction: The recorder now calls continuity() before appending and writes any missing eligible session, or any session recorded before eligibility, into data_quality_issues - which is itself chained.
payload.title: Continuity was never checked at record time
payload.what_was_wrong: A truncated prefix of a hash chain is itself a valid chain, so deleting trailing observations was undetectable. continuity() existed but was invoked only by phase4_checkpoint.py.

payload.affects: LIVE MONEY PATH - operational safety. No strategy rule changed.
payload.correction: broker.order(id) added: the order is the authority for its own fill. _entry_fills_this_cycle reads filled_qty for this cycle's entries; _settled_position_quantity refuses to trust a position read BELOW a known fill and re-reads up to 3 times, never returning more than the broker has shown (a stop for uncredited shares is rejected outright). _verify_stop_coverage re-reads positions AND working orders after the loop and classifies each position fully_protected / partially_protected / unprotected / stop_pending_verification, counting only orders the broker says are RESTING.
payload.reports_affected: none; no research result depends on live stop plumbing
payload.title: Protective-stop coverage race: stop sized from a stale position read
payload.what_was_wrong: On 2026-09-21 a BAC entry filled 229 shares at 19:48:20. Four seconds later /v2/positions still reported 219, _reconcile_protective_stops sized a GTC stop from that 219, and 10 shares had no protection for 17h42m across an overnight gap. The telemetry logged unprotected_remainder 0.0 because quantity and protectable both came from the SAME stale snapshot - the check certified itself.

payload.affects: operational log only; no trading decision, no clean-OOS record
payload.correction: The tests now write to an isolated temporary audit_log and state_file. The synthetic rows were ANNOTATED in place with an audit_log_contamination_notice record and NOT deleted; removing operational evidence to make a log read cleanly is the failure this project audits against.
payload.title: Unit tests wrote synthetic safety events into the live audit log
payload.what_was_wrong: While developing REM-0007 I ran tests whose AutoTradeConfig still used the default audit_log, appending 34 fake rows to data/autotrade-audit.jsonl at 15:34:31 and 15:35:28 - including rows reading 'BAC unprotected 229'. Those describe a fixture broker, not the account.
